title: When would you specifically need StringBuffer over StringBuilder?
shortTitle: When would you specifically need StringBuffer over StringBuilder?
keyPoints: Almost never in modern Java – StringBuilder + thread-local design is preferred
StringBuffer only when multiple threads SHARE the same mutable string builder
Even then, higher-level synchronization or thread-local builders are cleaner
Legacy code may use StringBuffer – do not change to StringBuilder without analyzing thread safety

s1_definition.oneliner: Almost never. Use StringBuilder by default. StringBuffer is only needed when multiple threads share the same builder instance, which is rare and usually a design smell.
s1_definition.profdef:
Decision:

- **StringBuilder:** Default choice. Single-threaded or thread-local building.
- **StringBuffer:** Only when the exact same builder instance is accessed by multiple threads simultaneously.
- **Better alternative:** Each thread builds with its own StringBuilder. No sharing, no synchronization.
s1_definition.analogy: When do you need a shared whiteboard with a lock (StringBuffer)? Almost never. Give each person their own whiteboard (StringBuilder). Faster and simpler.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Need string building?
    ├── Single thread? → StringBuilder (default)
    ├── Multi-thread, separate builders? → StringBuilder (each thread has its own)
    └── Multi-thread, SHARED builder? → StringBuffer (rare, usually wrong design)
                                         Better: thread-local builders + merge
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Use StringBuilder by default. StringBuffer is needed only when multiple threads share the same builder instance, which is rare and usually a design problem. Modern code uses thread-local builders or proper logging frameworks instead.

One sentence to remember: StringBuilder always, StringBuffer almost never – give each thread its own builder.
